stemMd: An editor argues that a biography is inaccurate because it contradicts an earlier biography that used the subject's private diaries. Which assumption would most support the inference?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Both biographies discuss the same historical period.

options.label: B
options.textMd: On the disputed points, the earlier biography faithfully represents diaries that accurately record the relevant events.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The subject intended the diaries for publication.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The newer biography contains more pages.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The newer author read the earlier biography.

explanationMd: Contradiction proves at most that both accounts cannot be correct on the same point. To select the newer account as inaccurate, the argument needs the earlier account to be reliable precisely where they conflict.

distractorRationale.d: Length does not resolve the contradiction.
distractorRationale.c: Intention alone does not establish accuracy.
distractorRationale.e: Awareness of a source does not establish which account is correct.
distractorRationale.a: Shared scope establishes comparability but not truth.
